key_insight: This paper extends causal discovery beyond regularly sampled data, enabling PCMCI+ to work on irregular time series. The result is a more practical way to uncover causal relationships in real-world event streams like sensors, healthcare records, and financial data.
problem_solved: Most causal discovery methods assume evenly spaced observations and fixed lag structures, which breaks down for irregularly sampled time series. This paper addresses the challenge of learning causal structure when events arrive at uneven times.
method: Builds on PCMCI+, a strong causal discovery method for multivariate time series.
Adapts the method to handle irregular sampling instead of requiring regular time intervals.
Targets event-driven data settings where timestamps are uneven and standard lag-based assumptions do not hold.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes causal discovery usable in many messy real-world datasets that were previously hard to analyze. It can improve interpretation, root-cause analysis, and decision-making in domains with irregular event logs.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of regular vs. irregular time series sampling

paper_title: Causal Discovery on Irregular Time Series
paper_authors: Martim Penim, Ricardo Ribeiro Pereira, Jacopo Bono, Hugo Ferreira, Mário A. T. Figueiredo
